cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still preaching to all Israel. Now he tells them these are the commandments the LORD told him to teach them. They're meant to be lived out in the land Israel is about to enter and possess.

cards.question: Moses says keeping these commands is how Israel will fear the LORD all their days. Who does he say should fear the LORD this way?

answers.text: Them and their children and grandchildren
Only the men of fighting age
Only the heads of each family

cards.text: Then Moses calls out, "Hear, O Israel…" and tells them to be careful to obey, with a promise from the LORD riding on it. He's basically tapping the microphone: "Is this thing on? ISRAEL!"

cards.question: True or false: Moses tells Israel to be careful to obey so they may prosper and multiply greatly in a land flowing with milk and honey.

cards.text: And then, right away, that line again: "Hear, O Israel…" Friend, when somebody tells you to listen twice in a row, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: Then comes the big line Moses wants Israel to hear. What does he say about the LORD their God?

answers.text: The LORD rests on the mountain

cards.question: Right after that, Moses tells Israel to love the LORD their God. What does he say to love Him with?

answers.text: All their heart and soul and strength

cards.text: ALL of it, friend, not the leftovers after a long shift at work. Then Moses says these words he's commanding today are to be upon their hearts.
He tells them to teach these words diligently to their children and to speak of them.

cards.question: True or false: Moses tells Israel to speak of these words mainly on the Sabbath.

cards.text: Moses says talk about them at home, on the road, when you lie down and when you get up. Friend, that's not a schedule, that's the whole DAY.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to tie these words as ___ on their hands and bind them on their foreheads.
Moses wants these words at home too. True or false: He tells Israel to write them on the doorposts of their houses and on their gates.

cards.text: Now Moses looks ahead to the day the LORD brings them into the land He swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Israel's forefathers. Great, splendid cities are waiting there, and Israel didn't build a single one.

cards.question: Moses keeps listing what's waiting for Israel in the land. What else does he say is already there for them?

answers.text: Wells and vineyards and olive groves
Herds of cattle and flocks of sheep

cards.text: Plus houses full of every good thing, like moving in and finding the cookie jar already stocked. But once they've eaten and they're satisfied, Moses has a warning.

cards.question: Once Israel is full and satisfied in the new land, what does Moses tell them to be careful not to do?

cards.text: Don't forget the LORD who brought them out of Egypt. Funny thing about being full, friend: you start thinking you baked those cookies yourself.

cards.question: True or false: Moses tells Israel to fear the LORD their God, serve Him only and take their oaths in His name.
Moses warns Israel not to follow other gods. Whose gods does he name?

cards.text: The LORD, who is among them, is a jealous God, Moses says. Otherwise His anger will be kindled against them, and He will wipe them off the face of the earth.
Then Moses brings up Massah, where Israel had no water and asked, "Is the LORD among us or not?" (Exodus 17:1, 7). Friend, this is not a fond-memories moment.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel not to ___ the LORD their God as they did at Massah.
Moses tells Israel to diligently keep the LORD's commands and do what is right and good in His sight. What does he say comes of that?

answers.text: It goes well and they possess the land
They become the rulers over Egypt
Their enemies make peace with them

cards.question: True or false: As Moses describes it, taking the land includes driving out all their enemies before them.

cards.text: Then Moses looks down the road. Someday a son is going to ask what all these decrees and statutes and ordinances actually mean.

cards.question: When a son asks what all the LORD's laws mean, Moses says the answer starts with this: they were ___ of Pharaoh, Egypt's king.

cards.text: Chip, one of my cookie cutter kids, always begged for one more story, and this answer IS a story. The LORD brought them out with a mighty hand, and before their eyes He inflicted great and devastating signs and wonders on Egypt, on Pharaoh and on all his household.
He brought them out from there to lead them in and give them the land He had sworn to their fathers.

cards.question: True or false: The answer to the son says the LORD's statutes were only for the people who came out of Egypt.

cards.text: The answer ends like this: if they're careful to observe every one of these commandments before the LORD, as He commanded, "then that will be our righteousness." Moses is just warming up the oven, friend, and this sermon is NOT done.
